title: 'Mattoon is too big for that': Residents share concerns after golf cart ordinance passed - NewsBreak
text: MATTOON, Ill. (WCIA) — People in Mattoon are sharing their concerns over the new golf cart ordinance. On Tuesday, WCIA reported that the Mattoon City Council unanimously approved an ordinance allowing golf carts to operate throughout the city. But, some community members are concerned because of the danger of having golf carts on the streets with cars, trucks, and SUV’s. One resident said the danger is his biggest worry. He doesn’t want to see kids driving up and down the road and getting hurt. “I think Mattoon is too big for that. I just look at the safety. Motorcycles are hard enough to see [without] worrying about golf carts. And then you don’t know who’s going to be on them,” Joseph Hopgood said. The city council said golf carts can be operated throughout the city where the posted speed limit is 30 miles per hour or less. One general manager of a company said he understands no one is comfortable with change but the new rule could benefit the community. “You know, as long as the right rules and regulations are in place, it’s actually something that’s considered to be very safe. It’s something that’s fun, it’s affordable. It’s safe for the environment,” Adam Fifield, Pilson Powersports general manager, said. The ordinance will make it illegal to drive golf carts on sidewalks and bike paths. Golf carts would also need to have specific equipment and safety features such as a rearview mirror, seatbelts, and turn signals. The Illinois Department of Transportation will implement golf carts crossing signs by Aug. 1. Officials also said their goal is to be creative by having golf cart parades for the city and other events. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WCIA.com.
